summary: bound.PageOptions/mcpPageConfig carry a FirstPageOnlyFields list; workouts_list sets it to ["summary"]. A named field is kept only on a query's very first page (no incoming cursor) and dropped from every later page, so workouts_list's per-month workout histogram (confirmed live at ~1.5 KB) stops being repeated fixed overhead on every page a caller pages through -- but only for the unprojected default response. mcpToolPageResultText only forwards FirstPageOnlyFields to bound.go when the call had no "select"; an explicit select naming the field on a later page (e.g. select=data.id,summary) is a deliberate ask and must be honored, not silently stripped. A regen touching workouts_list's mcpPageConfig or mcpToolPageResultText's hasSelect handling must keep both halves.
reason: Live retesting found summary present unchanged on every cursor page of workouts_list, useful once on page 1 and pure repeated cost afterward -- flagged as an easy byte win on the one endpoint (workouts) whose sync/archive path is still unexercised in live testing. A Greptile review on the resulting PR then found the first implementation stripped summary unconditionally on later pages, including when a caller explicitly select'd it -- silently returning less than requested.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test/govulncheck and verify_skill.py all green. TestEndpointPageResponseFirstPageOnlyFieldsDroppedOnLaterPages drives a first-page/second-page pair through the real EndpointPageResponse call path and asserts summary present on page one, absent on page two, with other fields (total) unaffected on both. TestMCPToolPageResultTextRespectsExplicitSelectOfFirstPageOnlyField (added after the Greptile finding) confirms an explicit select naming summary on a resumed call keeps it, while the same call with no select still drops it.
